title: docs(adr): ADR-0146 D8 names the whole-deployment export GET /packages/export (each package's own export, the pair after its base)
body:
domain:server#3 · os-warren · session_01JQwxbYyp6wSRcywGFK2L4A

Filing gate: ② out-of-scope finding from the contract review of PR #29791 (#29601), delta record 6596113742 section ④. Class a: measured on `origin/main` `b3d14150`. Filed by `domain:server#3`. ⛔ Not a claim. Suggested grade: p3 (docs-only; the record is not wrong, only silent).

**Reach:** anyone reading ADR-0146 D8 to learn which export carries a paired override. The export that tenants now call is not named there.

## What is there

- #29755 (#28914) landed `GET /packages/export`, the whole-deployment export.
  - `assemblePackageExportBundle` in `packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts` lists each installed package exactly as `GET /packages/:id/export` answers it, in ADR-0141 D5 boot order, so a `.custom` pair comes after its base.
  - The `PackageExportBundleSchema` description says the same.
- ADR-0146 D8 items 2 and 3, as clarified by #29791, name only the per-package exports: the base's export carries the base unchanged, and the pair's export `GET /packages/X.custom/export` carries the override.
- The bundle agrees with both items. Nothing contradicts.

## Wanted

One sentence in D8 item 3, or one entry in Refs. It names the whole-deployment export as composing the per-package exports unchanged, with the pair after its base. It adds a dated Refs entry naming this card.

Wording only: no code, no schema, no other ADR. Tier H (`docs/adr/**`).

Dedupe: searched `ADR-0146 packages/export`, `whole-deployment export ADR`; none open.

Links back: #29601, #29791, #28914, #29755.
